title: SnorriCam
description: A SnorriCam fixes the camera to the performer's body so the body remains stable relative to frame while the world moves. A rig points back at the wearer: the face stays pinned, the environment pitches around it.

sections.title: Narrative function

blocks.text: Trap the audience in a body that cannot get out. Panic, intoxication, or dissociation becomes spatial because the person is locked to the image and the street will not sit still.
It is the wrong tool for a first-person view of what they see. A SnorriCam faces the wearer.
It is not a body-cam showing the world, and it is not a follow from behind.

sections.title: How it works

blocks.text: Use a safely fitted lightweight body rig, or reproduce the relative motion in a virtual scene. Preserve tiny bodily movements without letting the face float independently of the torso.
Prompt a SnorriCam body-mounted on the subject, camera locked to the torso, face pinned, world sloshing behind.

sections.title: When to use it

blocks.text: Use it to trap the audience in a body that cannot get out. Concrete beat: a panicked walk down a sidewalk, pupils steady in frame, storefronts shearing.
Do not use it as POV of the sidewalk.

sections.title: Compared with similar shots

blocks.text: Point of View shows what they look at, from beside or as them. Handheld is an operator nearby, not bolted to the chest.
Locked-On glues the camera to a subject that may not be the wearer, often from outside a vehicle or a fall. SnorriCam is body-mounted and facing the actor.
Point of ViewForce identification. The audience is the character.

sections.title: In film

blocks.text: Requiem for a Dream uses body-mounted shots during panic and disorientation. Pi destabilizes Max's movement through the city with a pinned face.
Mean Streets is part of the same body-rig family. Face stable, world not: that is the grammar.

sections.title: Prompt it

blocks.text: SnorriCam body-mounted on [Subject], camera locked to the torso so the face stays pinned while the world sloshes behind, subjective intoxication or panic. For motion: body-mounted camera locked to [Subject]'s torso.
The face stays centered while the background slides wildly.

A frightened commuter walks quickly through a tiled tunnel. Body-mounted camera facing him: face and shoulders stay locked in the center while the corridor tilts and bobs with every step. Wide-angle proximity, natural strain, no free camera orbit and no normal handheld tracking.

sections.title: What usually goes wrong

blocks.text: The usual wrong cousin is Point of View or a Follow Shot from behind. The tell is seeing the street as the actor would, or seeing their back.
The fix: camera on the body, pointed at the face, background shearing.

sections.title: Questions

blocks.text: What is SnorriCam in film?
It is a camera rigged to the performer and aimed at them, so their face stays oddly stable while the environment moves around it.
SnorriCam vs Point of View
POV shows what the person sees. SnorriCam shows the person, locked to their torso, with the world unmoored behind them.
When should I use SnorriCam?
When panic, drugs, or dissociation should trap us in a body. Do not use it as a helmet-cam of the street.
How do I prompt SnorriCam for AI image or video?
Write body-mounted camera locked to the torso, face centered and pinned, background sliding wildly. Ban POV of the environment.
